paragraphs: Poulet basquaise surrounds browned chicken with piperade—soft peppers, onion, tomato, Espelette chile, and often cured Bayonne-style ham—from the Basque border region.

Poulet basquaise means Basque-style chicken. Its defining partner is piperade, the French Basque pepper-onion-tomato preparation; Bayonne ham and piment d'Espelette deepen regional identity. The English clarifier keeps the traditional name understandable at a glance. Navarin is simply a French lamb stew; navarin printanier is its spring-vegetable form. The English clarifier prevents the traditional title from signaling unnecessary complexity.
